key_insight: Large language models can sound clinically thoughtful yet still fail because they do not consistently seek the missing information needed to make a correct diagnosis or treatment decision.
clinical_relevance: In hematologic oncology, safe model use depends less on raw medical knowledge and more on whether the model can actively request key tests and patient data under uncertainty.
method: Models had to request clinical data over 3 sequential rounds before giving a diagnosis and treatment plan
32 frontier models were assessed with accuracy, information utilization, and reasoning-trace scoring
evidence_signal: The best model reached 68% overall accuracy, and information utilization was the strongest predictor of accuracy (R = 0.69, P < 0.001), but utilization dropped from 57% to 26% in the final round.
watch_item: High-quality reasoning traces did not reliably mean correct decisions, so deployment should not rely on explanations alone and should be limited until models improve information-seeking behavior.
paper_title: Information-seeking failures of large language models in agentic clinical reasoning
